venue: Ben Hill Griffin Stadium, Gainesville FL
title: Week 1 vs FAU
dek: Faulkner’s identity on the clips. White’s call sheet by down. What held. What leaked.
watchNote: PROVISIONAL — clip-chart draft for Charles. Official PBP = condensed snaps. Fan rail stays empty.
headline: Faulkner’s whole sell is run it when the stadium knows, get the ball to people in space, and make the quarterback pull the trigger. Saturday’s clips are that offense. White’s sell is four down, move the front, rush without emptying the shell. Saturday’s clips are that defense too — and the reason it played 90 snaps.

offense.body:
What makes Faulkner one of the best is not a trick play. FootballScoop named him National Offensive Coordinator of the Year at Georgia Tech last year — 466 yards a game, 7.09 a snap. He calls it a pro-style hybrid with Air Raid roots: same look, different answer, get the fastest people the ball, and run it when everybody in the building knows the run is coming. He is hard on the quarterback. Trust the leverage. Rip it. Do not sit on it.

The clip chart is 60 Florida snaps. Fifty-nine are shotgun. Thirty-eight are runs. Twenty-one are throws. That is the identity, not a slogan. First down they ran it 22 times and threw it 10. They handed it to Baugh when FAU was in the box and when FAU was not. The 61 is third-and-2 and they still gave it to him. The 18 is the bounce when the first hole died. The 12-yard score and the 7-yard score are the same back, downhill, after the throw has already been real. That is “run it when they know.”

The space part is the other half. Brown’s 49 is a short throw because the corner is off, then a miss, then grass. Stockton from the 12 is the same family — catch at the 11, finish. Wilson 19. Harpring 19. Clark leaking for 10 when the linebackers stay in on the run. Abrams 63 is the vertical answer after they finally crowd Baugh. Philo is 16 of 21, no sacks. The ball is out. That is Faulkner’s quarterback rule on the tape.

Where it leaked: the snap over Baugh’s head inside the five, 20 yards the wrong way. Philo’s rush for minus-2. The pick before the half — the ball comes off Mays, Sweeney has it. Third-and-7, they needed the trigger, they did not get the completion. Clark still had to make the tackle on the return.

What they did well: the run was the play, the quick throw was on time, the skill people stayed on blocks, and they still scored after their own mess. What to clean: the snap, the one late ball, and do not let a 20-yard loss become the clip Campbell puts on the board.
bullets: Identity on the chart: shotgun, run first (38–21), Baugh when they know.
Space: Brown after the catch, Stockton finish, Abrams when they crowd the run.
Philo pulls the trigger. The Mays–Sweeney ball is the one that stayed.
Clean the snap. Campbell will put that 20-yard loss on the tape.

defense.body:
White told the building what this defense is. Four down more than 3-4. JACK is a defensive end who can stand up. Move the three-technique so the offense cannot sit on one leverage. Get the run stopped. Pressure that does not empty the back end — four rushers, stunts, the STAR and the JACK, not a six-man every third down.

The clip chart is 90 FAU snaps. That number is the review. They did not get off the field.

Personnel: four down, extra defensive back on the inside receiver, corners with cushion. Graham and Chiles in the run and in the rush. Kanye Clark (STAR) is the first hurry on the night. McCloud, Bett, James, Lyons, Oyebadejo are the names on the hurries and sacks. That is the front and the STAR doing the work. The chart does not print “blitz.” It prints who got there.

Down and distance — when he sat, when he got home:

First down (35 snaps): four hurries, one sack (James, Veltkamp fumbles, FAU recovers), one pick (Johnson, Coleman on the breakup). They are playing the call. Short throws still convert. They sit in the shell and wait. The Johnson INT is first-and-10, FAU 25 — he held it, they took it.

Second down (26 snaps): four hurries (Bett twice, Kanye Clark, Oyebadejo). No sack. No pick. They are still four-man/STAR. FAU stays on schedule underneath.

Third down (22 snaps): one hurry (McCloud), one sack (Lyons and Graham), one pick (Coleman, third-and-10 at the Florida 35). That is White’s down. Get home or take the ball. They also lose the keep here — third-and-7 at the 7, Veltkamp walks in. JACK left the edge.

Fourth down (7 snaps): he does not hunt a hurry. He plays the down. McCloud breaks up 4th-and-2. James stops Ervin short on 4th-and-4. Bett rips 4th-and-1 from the 1. They also give 4th-and-4, 4th-and-1, and 4th-and-8 conversions on the short throw. Three stops. Four conversions. The short game is still the tax.

What they did well: the two interceptions are the plan — sit, make him hold it, Coleman and Johnson are in the window. The three fourth-down kills. James and Lyons in the backfield. Bett finishing the keep.

What to clean: 90 snaps. The pile at the 1. The end who leaves. The fade to Valsin when the corner is playing off. Sumrall already said atrocious. The film says the same thing in a quieter way — they played White’s call and they did not get off the field. Campbell will throw it short and run the quarterback. Same two jobs.
bullets: Personnel: four down, STAR on the slot, corners off. JACK has to be the end.
Pressure on the chart is STAR/DL/Chiles — first and second down hurries. Third down is the pick and the sack.
Fourth down: three stops, four conversions. Bett gets the last keep.
90 snaps. Pile, edge, fade. That is the improvement list.

specials.body: Fourth-and-4 at the FAU 35. They take the points. Durkin from 53. Florida never punts. No hidden specials story on this tape.

keys: Faulkner’s clips match the hire: run it when they know, throw it into space, Philo rips it.
White’s clips match the hire: four down, sit in the shell, take the held ball. They still played 90 snaps.
Plus: Baugh, the quick game, Coleman/Johnson, three fourth-down kills, Bett.
Clean: the snap, the edge, the pile, the fade, get off the field.

nextWeek.look: Sixkiller will throw it short and keep it. Faulkner will still run Baugh when they know. White has to get off the field on third and keep JACK home on the keep.
